solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Children keeping dog brought to safety

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A family's children keep the dog close as they are all led out of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children' is the old sense of seed, meaning offspring, as in 'the seed of Abraham'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made secure has been placed out of danger, as a rescued person is taken to a safe place.

clue.text: Military commander admitting oversight finally — one's fired

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a shogun was a Japanese military ruler

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A general admits a final oversight, and one man gets fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T, the end of 'oversight', and 'admitting' puts it inside SHOGUN. 'fired' suggests dismissal but means discharged as a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a firearm, a thing that is discharged with a shot.

clue.text: Mockery of politician in debate that hasn't succeeded

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, inside it
a word that hasn't the letter for succeeded is without it, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a contest is a debate or argument
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is mocked in a debate that has gone badly for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that hasn't' leaves CONTET once the S (succeeded, from family trees) goes; 'in' then houses the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn or disdain, the attitude shown when ridiculing someone.

clue.text: Reference compiler exposing nonsense about good English

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: A dictionary maker exposes rubbish written about good English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GE inside ROT. Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous thesaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget produced the Thesaurus of English Words and Phrases, a standard reference book.

clue.text: Rush to get mug in seaside location

parts.note: to dart is to rush
mug is slang for face, here the mouth

explanation.surface: Hurry off to buy a mug at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a cup but is slang for the face. Dartmouth is a town on the Devon coast, home of the naval college.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmouth is a coastal town in Devon, England, at the mouth of the River Dart.

clue.text: Zealot to rock around

indicators.note: turning around means the letters of the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, often shortened to Gib

explanation.surface: A fanatic is urged to go and rock about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns TOGIB backwards. Gibraltar is known as the Rock, and Gib is its everyday short name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is a person fanatically devoted to their own opinions, close to a zealot in sense.

clue.text: Quail, being left stuck in seat

indicators.note: something stuck in is pushed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a bench is a seat

explanation.surface: A quail is left stuck on a bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' puts L inside BENCH. 'Quail' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to flinch.
explanation.definitionFit: To blench is to flinch or shrink back in fear, as one does in quailing.

clue.text: Cook requires good little sieve

parts.note: G is the short form of good, the 'little' saying it is cut down
a riddle is a coarse sieve, used for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: A cook needs a good small sieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is the verb, meaning to cook on a flat iron plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To griddle food is to cook it on a griddle, a flat heated plate.

clue.text: Element hanging round game making one cross

indicators.note: to hang round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: tin is a chemical element
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: An element hanging about a game that makes someone angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but means a hybrid; 'hanging round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the offspring of a male tiger and a female lion, a hybrid animal.

clue.text: Five in a social event meeting duke, getting on

indicators.note: meeting means the next piece joins on after
one piece goes in the other, inside it

parts.note: a dance is a social event
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people at a dance meet a duke who is getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts V inside ADANCE to give ADVANCE, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced in years means old, the same as getting on, an idiom for ageing.

clue.text: Flood having subsided with river contained

indicators.note: something contained is held within, so the abbreviation goes inside the other word

parts.note: a thing that has subsided has gone down

explanation.surface: A flood that has gone down, with the river back within its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contained' puts R inside DOWN. The surface talks of floodwater going down, while the verb sense of 'Flood' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood land or a crop is to submerge it, the verb sense of covering it completely with water.

clue.text: Outdoor job travelling round forest, missing nothing

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it
missing means the letter for nothing is dropped

parts.note: travelling is going
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing
the Forest of Arden, the woodland setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A worker travels around a forest for an outdoor job, finding nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' leaves GING; 'round' wraps it about the Forest of Arden, Shakespeare's setting for As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending a garden is a typical task done outside, in the open air.

clue.text: Add to workers in holiday month with our lot off

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, being placed inside it
off means these letters are removed

parts.note: August is the main summer holiday month in Britain
our lot is us
workers are men, as in a gang of workmen

explanation.surface: More workers are taken on in August while our own team is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' leaves AUGT; 'in' then takes the workers. August is the main British summer holiday month.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to increase it, making it larger by adding more.

clue.text: Fellow holding church party in kingdom once

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fellow is a man
CE is the Church of England
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A man takes a church party to an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal; CE is the Church of England, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedon was an ancient Greek realm, the home of Alexander the Great, so a former monarchy.

clue.text: Survey revealing deception: sect's up for reform

parts.note: a con is a deception or swindle

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A report reveals a con, and a religious sect is due for an overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reform' rearranges SECTSUP into SPECTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspectus is a general overview or summary of a subject, as a survey is.

clue.text: A new shirt PC ordered — I'd retain his helmet?

definitions.note: the strap speaks, saying it would keep the police officer's helmet in place

indicators.note: to be ordered is to be put in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police constable orders a new shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges ANSHIRTPC. 'his' in the definition points back to the PC of the wordplay, whose helmet the strap holds on.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap under the jaw keeps headgear such as a police constable's helmet secure.

clue.text: Top style in Russian city

definitions.meaning: a hairstyle, the top being the head, with waves set chemically
a large city on the Kama River in the Urals

explanation.surface: A smart hairdo spotted in a Russian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent wave is a hairstyle, and Perm is a large city in Russia.

clue.text: Goodness gracious, having to get round exam on modern technology!

indicators.note: to get round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: My! and Gracious! are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Goodness gracious, a student must get round an exam on computing!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness gracious' reads as one exclamation, but only 'Goodness' is the definition; 'to get round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Morality is moral virtue, the quality of being good or right in conduct.

clue.text: Roman official's search round area to get gold

definitions.note: the 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a quest is a search
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A Roman official goes searching round an area for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal; OR for gold comes from heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaestor was a magistrate of ancient Rome in charge of public money.

clue.text: Chemist placing vanadium in period

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside
in says where the symbol is placed, inside the other word

parts.note: a day is a period of time
V is the chemical symbol for vanadium

explanation.surface: A chemist adds vanadium to his sample for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placing in' puts V inside DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Humphry Davy was an English scientist who isolated sodium and potassium and invented the miners' safety lamp.

clue.text: Six sandwiches bought up for guest

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: in a down clue a word brought up is read from the bottom upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: rotis are Indian flatbreads, here taken as wraps or sandwiches

explanation.surface: Six sandwiches are bought for a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bought up' turns ROTIS backwards. The blog reads this as 'brought up', the usual signal in a down clue; as printed here the word is 'bought'.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone who comes to see you, a guest in your home.

clue.text: School with top athlete

parts.note: a high school is a secondary school, often just called the High
a jumper is a knitted top, a sweater

explanation.surface: A school sports star in a smart top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like praise for the athlete but is a garment: a jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in the field event of leaping over a bar is one kind of athlete.

clue.text: Criminal offence of a group in court

parts.note: a means per, as in 'five pounds a head'
a jury is the group of citizens who hear a trial

explanation.surface: A group in court are found guilty of an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives PER as in 'ten pence a pound'.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury is lying under oath, a crime in law.

clue.text: Cheer coming from old men in dance

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, inside it

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A cheer goes up from old men at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'men' as OR (other ranks) is a crossword convention; the hay is an old rustic dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooray is a shout of joy or approval, the cry one raises in cheering.

clue.text: Game men with desire, heading off into dances

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, inside it

parts.note: bops are dances, in informal use

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for desire drops its first letter

parts.note: a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: Players with an urge to set off to the dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves ISH; 'into' places it in the dances. 'Game men' means chess pieces, not hunters.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the pieces that move diagonally are among the men of the game.

clue.text: Uncritical learner in tricky situation

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, inside it

parts.note: a bind is a difficult situation
L is a learner, as on the plates of a British learner driver

explanation.surface: A learner finds himself in an awkward spot, with no judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside BIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind faith or loyalty is unquestioning, accepted without critical judgement.

clue.text: Membrane's wrecked by a puller

definitions.note: an adjective, meaning of or belonging to the membrane round the lungs

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A membrane is torn by someone pulling at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges APULLER. The definition reads as an adjective: 'Membrane's' means belonging to the membrane, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleura is the membrane lining the chest around the lungs; the adjective means relating to it.

clue.text: Old man, head on verge of retirement

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head

indicators.note: the verge is the edge, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An old man whose head is on the brink of retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verge of' takes R, the first letter of 'retirement', and 'on' places PATE above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father, and old man is slang for one's father.

clue.text: What's provided by painter, pretty gloss

indicators.note: the answer is supplied by letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A painter puts a pretty gloss on his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'painter, pretty'. 'gloss' looks like paint but is the verb meaning to explain.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss a text is to explain its meaning, as an interpreter does.

clue.text: Guy in cricket side leaving Somerset's ground

indicators.note: leaving means these letters go out of the word

parts.note: Taunton is the home ground of Somerset County Cricket Club
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A man plays in a cricket team that has left its Somerset home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes ON out of TAUNTON. Somerset is an English county; its cricket team plays at Taunton. 'Guy' is the verb meaning to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to make fun of them, to jeer or ridicule.

clue.text: City match expecting many away supporters?

definitions.meaning: an English city in the East Midlands
a game between local rivals, whose away fans need travel only a short way, so many come

explanation.surface: A city club's game that should draw a big visiting crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A local derby is a match between two teams from the same area.
explanation.definitionFit: Derby is a city in England, and a derby is a game between neighbouring rival teams.

clue.text: Give description of fish coming to harbour

indicators.note: the fish comes to the harbour, so it follows that word

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Describe a fish swimming into harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to depict or represent it, in words or pictures.
